clue.text: Like an Aussie hobo, swallowing extremes of grog in time

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: first part of DAY, a unit of time

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of grog
end of DAY, closing round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: An Australian tramp knocking back the ends of his rum ration on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the cryptic reading 'in time' rather than being a separate signal; the period of time is the one that does the swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Daggy is Australian slang for scruffy or unkempt, the typical look of a swagman or tramp.

clue.text: Big drum that's bashed after noon for Mikado

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Mikado, a title of the emperor of Japan, taken as written
M stands for meridies, Latin for noon; it is the letter set aside

explanation.surface: A large drum is beaten in the afternoon to herald the Mikado's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer ('that'), bashed and placed after noon's letter, makes MIKADO. Working forwards, take noon's letter off Mikado and bash the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A daiko, better known as taiko, is a large Japanese drum beaten with sticks.

clue.text: A Euro-juju? Lor, that's odd, providing for immediate needs only (12, four words)

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange exclamation about European magic charms, as if spoken by a startled Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lor' is a dialect exclamation, short for Lord; it is all fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'from day to day', describing a hand-to-mouth existence that meets only present needs.

clue.text: Grand old knight provides assistance for travellers on the road

definitions.text: assistance for travellers on the road

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for grand
ritter is an archaic word for a knight, from German

explanation.surface: An elderly knight of noble rank helps wayfarers along the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: A gritter is a lorry that spreads grit or salt on icy British roads in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: By spreading grit on frozen roads the vehicle helps motorists keep traction, a service to road users.

clue.text: Denizens of the everglades chatter about rising putrescence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round another

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: rot is decay or putrescence

explanation.surface: Swamp creatures gossip about decay drifting upwards from the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas as a verb means to talk at length; in this down clue 'rising' turns the decay word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Gators is the informal short form of alligators, which live in Florida's Everglades swamps.

clue.text: Archetypal rustic, modest fellow? That's about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap round the next letter

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
R is the usual abbreviation for right
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A typical country bumpkin is a shy chap, and that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: COY DON, 'modest fellow', is wrapped about R: CO(R)Y DON.
explanation.definitionFit: Corydon is a shepherd in Virgil's Eclogues, and the name became the conventional one for any pastoral swain.

clue.text: Backward kids in school, a failure

indicators.note: backward means read in the opposite direction, from end to start

parts.note: children at school are pupils

explanation.surface: Slow learners in a classroom are written off as a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like an unkind description of the kids; it only tells you to read them in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a mistake or minor failure.

clue.text: Deep blue briny around Malta

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: first letter of SALT, as briny means salt
M is the international vehicle code for Malta
rest of SALT, closing round the inserted letter

explanation.surface: The deep blue salt sea surrounding the Mediterranean island of Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT goes round M: S(M)ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalt is a deep blue pigment made from powdered glass coloured with cobalt.

clue.text: Coarse abuse, son going for college

indicators.note: one letter going for another means it replaces it in the word

parts.note: to insult someone is to abuse them
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
C is an abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: Crude verbal abuse as a student leaves home for university.
explanation.walkthrough: In INSULT the S is swapped for C.
explanation.definitionFit: Incult is a rare word for uncultivated or unrefined, so rough and coarse in manner.

clue.text: Support king following church rule book

indicators.note: following places the king after the book, setting out the order of the parts

parts.note: the pie or pye was a pre-Reformation book of rules for church services
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Backing the monarch who follows the rules laid down by the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a solid pillar or column that supports an arch or bridge span.

clue.text: Classes tucked into tureen's stew, showing no compunction

indicators.note: something tucked into another is put inside it
a stew is a jumbled mixture, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive dropped
genera are classes in biological classification

explanation.surface: Cooking whole categories of food in a tureen's stew with no qualms at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of tureen's is surface glue; only the six letters of tureen are stewed, and the classes go inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Unregenerate means unrepentant or unreformed, so feeling no remorse or scruple.

clue.text: State of affairs ragged by troupes

indicators.note: to rag is to tease or knock about, so the letters are roughed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A situation being mocked by bands of travelling actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture can mean the current position or state of affairs, as in a country's defence posture.

clue.text: Colour therapy from USA, aroma varied

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alternative health treatment imported from America with a changing scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Aura-Soma is a system of alternative healing using coloured oils in bottles, a form of colour therapy.

clue.text: Opening of public bar, distinguished scientists in jumpers

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of public
rance is a Scots word for a bar or prop
RS is the Royal Society, Britain's academy of eminent scientists

explanation.surface: At the opening of a pub's bar, eminent scientists appear wearing woolly sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' suggests British sweaters, but it means leaping animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Prancers are horses that spring and caper, so they are jumpers in the leaping sense.

clue.text: Bow elaborately played took lead in Weber

indicators.note: played suggests something performed freely, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of took rearranged

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Weber

explanation.surface: A musician bowed deeply after taking the lead in a piece by the composer Weber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' and 'played' together suggest a violinist, but bow here is the bending kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Kotow is a variant of kowtow, the Chinese custom of kneeling and touching the forehead to the ground.

clue.text: US tableware? Alas, this cruet we smashed

indicators.note: something smashed is broken to pieces, so its letters can be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written; it is the result of the broken letters
taken as written, part of the shuffled set
taken as written, part of the shuffled set

explanation.surface: A sad confession: we broke this American-made condiment cruet at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositional anagram: ALAS + answer + WE, smashed, gives US TABLEWARE, so taking ALAS and WE out of those letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Buret is the American spelling of burette, which Chambers also gives as a cruet used for church wine or water.

clue.text: Fantastic diamonds are topping in rubescence

parts.note: outré means bizarre or fantastic
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Extraordinary diamonds are the best thing in a blushing red display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an adjective for excellent; it is a verb, to top or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To outred is to exceed in redness, and rubescence is the quality of reddening.

clue.text: South Indian lute played with kind of viol

indicators.note: an instrument played is handled freely, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of lute rearranged
the gu or gue is an old Shetland violin

explanation.surface: A musician from southern India strums a lute alongside a type of viol.
explanation.definitionFit: Telugu is a Dravidian language and people of Andhra Pradesh in south-east India.

clue.text: Specialized artist, scribbled score held in clenched hand

indicators.note: held in means gripped inside another word
something scribbled is written messily, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of score rearranged
a fist is a clenched hand

explanation.surface: A composer gripping a hastily written musical score in his fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' sounds like the music the artist holds; it is only the letters to be scribbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A frescoist is a painter who works in fresco, on wet plaster, a specialised branch of painting.

clue.text: National costume? Trademark's mostly seen in dress

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside another word

parts.note: fig means dress or array, as in full fig

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a label is a brand or trademark

explanation.surface: A designer label prominently displayed on a country's traditional outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Fig means dress, as in the phrase 'in full fig', meaning in full formal attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A filabeg is a Highland kilt, the national dress of Scotland; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Fine Shakespearean as part of Sebastian touring Ulster?

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: in means being part of something
first part of COE, after Sebastian Coe the British runner
Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
end of COE, closing round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A fine Shakespearean actor playing Sebastian on a tour of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a British Olympic middle-distance champion. IN + CO(NI)E; Sebastian is also a Shakespearean role, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconie, or incony, is a word Shakespeare uses in Love's Labour's Lost meaning fine or delicate.

clue.text: Scottish cuckoo? Caught in net it's lacking in value

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside another word

parts.note: first part of GOAL, the net in football

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: merit is worth or value
taken as written, the letters removed
end of GOAL, closing round the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A Scottish bird trapped in a mist net is of little worth.
explanation.walkthrough: MERIT without IT is MER, caught in GOAL: GO(MER)AL. 'Cuckoo' means a fool here, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomeral is a Scots word for a fool or simpleton, and cuckoo is slang for a crazy person.

clue.text: Spooner's rabbit call? It can set you tingling (9, two words)

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the opening sounds are exchanged

to phone is to call; its first sound swaps with the previous word's

explanation.surface: A rabbit's ringing telephone call could make you tingle with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking the elbow at the funny bone hits the ulnar nerve and sends a tingling jolt down the arm.

clue.text: Turkey kept in fridge (for Laurence) where brothers live

end of FRAY, closing round the inserted letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fridge' is not the refrigerator but Sterne's word meaning to fray or chafe; FRA(TR)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A fratry is a monastery's frater, the house or quarters of a religious brotherhood of friars.

clue.text: Sea's holding nothing for a climber

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: the briny is a name for the sea

explanation.walkthrough: BRINY holds O: BRI(O)NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Briony, or bryony, is a hedgerow plant that climbs by tendrils.

clue.text: The French jaunt? Give it all you've got (6, two words)

parts.note: le is French for the
a trip is a jaunt

explanation.surface: Urging a French holiday-maker on their outing to go flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is to act without restraint, putting full energy or force into it.

clue.text: Lowly worker in part following leader of party

indicators.note: following places one piece after another, setting the order
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of party
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A humble labourer playing a role behind the party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Prole, short for proletarian, is an informal word for a working-class labourer.

clue.text: Small underground stem, a feature of garlic or melilot

parts.note: the letters running across the boundaries of these words

clue.text: Source of oil from Japan, sealed in a pasty

indicators.note: sealed in means enclosed inside another word

parts.note: taken as written

pasty means pale-faced, wan

clue.text: Short poem? Sounds like a whopper

clue.text: Former spouse, violent, not cold inside

clue.text: W. Indian opener bagging runs, object of quest of old

R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
rest of GAYLE, closing round the inserted letter

clue.text: Ten's first at start — count backwards — uprising followed me

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of Ten

indicators.note: backwards means read from end to start

parts.note: to rely is to count, as in count on someone

explanation.surface: A countdown from ten heralds a revolt that I led.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381. 'Count backwards' suggests a countdown; it means RELY read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking as Wat Tyler: the Peasants' Revolt was the uprising that followed his leadership.
